result.summary: This PR removes a legacy 'reverse precedence' code path in ArgsManager::GetSetting that previously made config-file settings take the value of the first assignment instead of the last. The author states this has no behavior effect because a prior PR (#17493) already made it an error to assign a single-value setting multiple times in the same config section. It is the final commit in a long stack (#16545, #17580, #17493) that reworks ArgsManager type/flag handling and settings merging, and is explicitly part of the 'Simpler settings interpretation' cleanup project (#17508).
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's config-file settings merge logic has an inconsistent, hard-to-reason-about precedence rule (first-wins for config-file settings, last-wins everywhere else) that exists only for legacy compatibility. This PR removes the now-unreachable special case so future contributors working on ArgsManager/settings do not have to reason about it.

result.card: This PR removes a legacy 'reverse precedence' quirk in ArgsManager's settings-merge logic, stating it has no behavior effect now that a prior PR (#17493) forbids multiple config-file assignments to single-value settings. It is the top commit of a long stack (#16545, #17580, #17493), part of the author's 'Simpler settings interpretation' cleanup project (issue #17508). The PR has been open since 2019, force-pushed 21 times purely for rebasing, and has never received a single review comment (Crickets). It remains a draft and depends on three other unmerged base PRs, so review is best started at the base of the stack. Impact is limited to internal settings-code clarity (utils, P3); no user-facing behavior changes are claimed or evident.
